# Corrected concision guidance and corpus-supported signal discovery

Date: 2026-09-03. Work ticket: inanimate-unrideable-wasp (ee2e-6fec-aa8a-4e77).

## Correction and evidentiary bar

The prior production recommendation is withdrawn. R1–R10 were not “unvalidated signals”; the reported historical data refuted them for production use. A signal is not useful merely because it has high specificity on an all-negative sample. For this work, a candidate must have TP > 0 and TP > FP on historical tickets. Production adoption additionally requires a frozen held-out evaluation and evidence that acting on the flag preserves protected facts and fresh-agent resumption.

The original results remain:

| Rule | TP | FP | FN | TN | Disposition |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| R1 exact duplication | 1 | 1 | 1 | 17 | Refuted: FP = TP |
| R2 near/history duplication | 0 | 0 | 4 | 16 | Refuted: no TP |
| R3 transcript dump | 0 | 0 | 0 | 20 | Refuted: no positive case |
| R4 empty update | 0 | 0 | 0 | 17 | Refuted: no positive case |
| R5 filler/meta | 0 | 0 | 0 | 20 | Refuted: no positive case |
| R6 sentence/paragraph sprawl | 6 | 14 | 0 | 0 | Refuted: FP > TP |
| R7 alternatives/hedges | 0 | 0 | 0 | 20 | Refuted: no positive case |
| R8 imperative saturation | 0 | 0 | 2 | 18 | Refuted: no TP |
| R9 length envelope | 5 | 13 | 0 | 2 | Refuted: FP > TP |
| R10 canonical copying | 0 | 0 | 2 | 17 | Refuted: no TP |

The naive union was TP 6, FP 14, FN 0, TN 0. Do not block, warn, or coach from these rules. In particular, length, sentence size, imperative density, alternatives, and generic duplication are not evidence of bloat across artifact types.

## Shared agent instruction

First identify the artifact and its future reader. Write the minimum sufficient record for that artifact. Preserve facts needed to execute, verify, decide, audit, troubleshoot, or resume: current state, chosen path, constraints, identifiers, paths, commands, exact values/dates/errors, measurements, evidence, blockers, and exact next action. Lead with the outcome or delta. Link bulky or canonical evidence when the target reader can retrieve it. Remove a semantic unit only when its removal does not impair the artifact’s purpose.

Use a final compression pass: mark units KEEP, COMPRESS, or DELETE; protect the facts above; merge repeated propositions; then verify that a fresh agent can recover current state, chosen path, constraints, proof, blocker, and exact next action. “Owner” is intentionally not part of this check.

## Artifact-specific contracts

### Executable ticket descriptions and plans

Applies to task, story, bug, and epic descriptions used to execute work. Keep the problem/outcome, scope boundaries, one chosen implementation path, dependencies, constraints, measurable acceptance criteria, and verification. Once a path is selected, omit unchosen alternatives; link the ADR or research record that owns the decision. Keep one authoritative current plan: consolidate remediation into it instead of appending another plan or acceptance-criteria block. Investigation chronology and raw evidence belong in a linked session log or incident record. Do not repeat the same contract separately as approach, scope, testing, and acceptance criteria unless each occurrence adds a distinct executable predicate.

### Ticket comments and handoffs

Comments record a delta: new evidence, decision, blocker, state transition, or exact next action. Do not recap the ticket or replay completed work. A correction may quote the minimum text needed to identify what it supersedes. A handoff contains current state, chosen path, constraints, proof, blocker, and exact resumption action; history stays linked.

### ADRs and decision records

Alternatives are load-bearing here. Record the decision context, decision criteria, chosen option, seriously considered alternatives, why each was rejected, consequences, reversibility, and evidence. Compression must not erase trade-offs needed to revisit the decision. Move executable steps to tickets and long experimental chronology to research/session artifacts.

### User-facing documentation

Optimize for successful user tasks and accurate mental models, not minimum length. Include prerequisites, ordered instructions, examples, expected results, warnings at the point of risk, and troubleshooting for likely failures. Alternative paths are appropriate when users genuinely face different environments or goals. Use progressive disclosure: a short primary path with linked advanced, conceptual, and troubleshooting material. Remove internal agent/tool narration and repeated background that does not help a user act.

### Reference and API documentation

Completeness, stable lookup, and exact contracts take priority. Parameters, return values, defaults, errors, compatibility, examples, and edge cases may require repeated local context because readers enter at arbitrary sections. Prefer schemas, tables, generated references, and canonical cross-links over prose repetition. Do not apply ticket-length or alternatives rules.

### Incident and security records

Preserve chronology, timestamps, affected identities/systems, exact safe-to-record errors, hypotheses tested, negative results, mitigations, hashes, evidence, and residual risk. Rejected hypotheses and repeated safety constraints can be necessary audit evidence. Put a concise current-state/RCA summary first and detailed evidence below or in linked appendices. Never reproduce secrets.

### Session logs and research notes

These are the sanctioned home for verbose chronology, raw or linked evidence, intermediate hypotheses, and source notes. Add a concise summary/index and durable links so other artifacts can point here rather than copy it. Do not judge them by executable-ticket density.

## 2026 research and OSS interpretation

The cited 2026 studies support selective compression, explicit preservation classes, and downstream-cost evaluation—not universal terseness. PACE (arXiv:2607.11266) distinguishes valid content from necessary content. The Sleeping Agent (arXiv:2608.11775) shows gist compression can destroy temporal facts unless preservation is explicit. Context Compression Cost (arXiv:2608.16370) shows apparent task success can hide extra retrieval work, and arXiv:2605.11051 warns that compression that works for single-shot understanding can fail in multi-step software work. The alternatives result in arXiv:2607.17063 applies to over-answering/Q&A; it does not justify deleting considered alternatives from ADRs, troubleshooting branches from user documentation, or rejected hypotheses from incidents.

The maintained OSS examples—OpenAI and Anthropic skill creators, obra/superpowers, Anthropic Claude Code review prompts, and GitHub Awesome Copilot—converge on progressive disclosure, canonical references, output schemas/examples, and confidence/evidence gating. Their numeric caps and terse personas are project conventions, not evidence for universal ticket thresholds.

## New deterministic candidates supported on the frozen corpus

These candidates apply only to compiled executable-ticket records. They were discovered/refined on the same 20 labeled tickets, so the numbers below are resubstitution evidence. An independent background reviewer re-fetched all 20 tickets through MCP and reproduced every fire and count.

### S1 — revision residue

Fire when either:

1. A description has at least three outside-fence H2 headings whose normalized titles begin `Acceptance Criteria`; or
2. A comment is at least 75% of the current description’s Unicode-character length and its first 400 Unicode characters match, case-insensitively: `full original (description|plan)`; `original (description|plan)` followed within 80 characters by `preserv` or `verbatim`; or `pre[- ]condensation (draft|description)`.

Observed fires: outrageous-uncultured-wildebeest, stew-kid-motif, lofty-beech-twang. Matrix: TP 3 (15%), FP 0, FN 3 (15%), TN 14 (70%); precision 100%, recall 50%, specificity 100%.

### S2 — cross-section echo saturation

Partition outside-fence H2 sections into design (Approach/Implementation), scope (Scope/File impact), verification (Testing/Test plan), and acceptance (Acceptance Criteria). All four families must exist. Fire when either:

1. There are at most six acceptance checklist items and one identical backticked CamelCase token occurs in all four families; or
2. One identical backticked, non-URL, no-whitespace local path containing `/` occurs in all four families, and at least three distinct such paths each occur in at least three families.

Observed fires: enduring-cagophilic-orca and blousy-luxuriant-rasbora. Matrix: TP 2 (10%), FP 0, FN 4 (20%), TN 14 (70%); precision 100%, recall 33.3%, specificity 100%.

### S3 — truncated acceptance residue

Within any outside-fence H2 Acceptance Criteria section, fire on at least three physically adjacent unchecked checklist starter lines when each line, after stripping trailing Markdown delimiters, ends with comma, plus, or one of: `of`, `and`, `or`, `with`, `using`, `to`, `the`, `a`, `an`, `for`, `from`, `into`. “Physically adjacent” is required; wrapped checklist items with intervening continuation lines do not count.

Observed fire: dissimilar-sorcerous-hartebeest. Matrix: TP 1 (5%), FP 0, FN 5 (25%), TN 14 (70%); precision 100%, recall 16.7%, specificity 100%.

The OR of S1–S3 fires on exactly all six adjudicated bloated tickets: TP 6, FP 0, FN 0, TN 14. This perfect fit must not be represented as generalization: the predicates were selected after observing this sample. Batch-local candidate discovery produced no true positive outside the discovering batch, so there is not yet an independent positive validation case.

## Production decision and next gate

R1–R10 are rejected. S1–S3 are the only current corpus-supported candidates, but are not safe to enforce or ship as warnings yet. Freeze their exact definitions, then evaluate them without tuning on a new historical holdout that includes ordinary-length tickets, long descriptions, comment-heavy tickets, and enough independently adjudicated positive cases. Require TP > 0 and TP > FP on the holdout. Before automatic coaching, rewrite flagged tickets and verify protected-fact retention, fresh-agent resumption, and no increase in history rereads/tool calls. Apply the same admission bar to any LLM criterion, with matched spans and a specific removable-content explanation.

## Artifacts
